report.source_text: External examination showed slight proptosis and upward displacement of the right eye (Fig. 1). There was no palpable mass in periorbital area. Hertel exophthalmometry revealed a 3 mm proptosis on the right side. Globe mobility was complete in the left eye, but infraduction and supraduction was comprimised in the right eye. Slit lamp, fundoscopic, Humphrey visual fields and visual evoked potential examinations of both eyes were unremarkable. The intraocular pressure measured by Goldmann tonometer was 15 mm Hg in both eyes.

report.source_text: Orbital computed tomography (CT) scanning showed enlargement of the right inferior rectus muscle infiltrated by a muscle-density tumor which was about 11 × 17 × 7 mm3 that displaced the globe upward. An axial magnetic resonance images (MRI) view of the orbit revealed a nodule-like tumor derived from the inferior rectus muscle, which was slightly hypo-intense to the extraocular muscles on T1W with a very low central intensity on T2W and a higher intensity along the periphery. Sagittal MRI images showed that the tumor was very close to the optic nerve with almost no gap in between. Enhanced MRI after intravenous contrast administration showed that the tumor was significantly enhanced in the periphery but only slight enhanced in the center (Fig. 2).

report.source_text: The tumor was surgically removed via a transconjunctival approach along inferior rectus muscle. Intraoperatively, the tumor was completely separated from muscle tissue since it was pseudoencapsular. The gross specimen exhibited a firm fibrotic nodule-like and pale-colored mass (Fig. 3). There was no significant improvement in globe mobility after surgery; however, a longer term follow-up is required.

clinician.final_diagnosis: GCT (Giant Cell Tumor of the inferior rectus muscle/tendon sheath)
clinician.trajectory_summary: A 45-year-old man presented with 3-year progressive vertical diplopia and severe visual impairment in upgaze (hand motion/10cm) but normal acuity in primary gaze (20/20). Examination revealed 3mm right proptosis with upward globe displacement and restricted infraduction/supraduction. CT imaging demonstrated an 11×17×7 mm muscle-density tumor infiltrating the right inferior rectus muscle with upward globe displacement. MRI characterized the lesion as arising from the inferior rectus, hypointense on T1-weighted images, with very low central intensity and higher peripheral intensity on T2-weighted images, and peripheral enhancement with slight central enhancement post-contrast, abutting the optic nerve. Surgical excision via a transconjunctival approach revealed a pseudoencapsulated, firm fibrotic nodule that was completely separated from the muscle tissue. Histopathology confirmed an encapsulated tumor with nested/cord-like cells, small nuclei, and abundant eosinophilic cytoplasm, with immunohistochemistry showing CD68+, S100+, vimentin+, weak Ki67 positivity, and CK negativity, consistent with Giant Cell Tumor. Post-operatively, there was no significant improvement in globe mobility, with long-term follow-up planned.
